doc.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025

title: Favorite bassists and influences
summary: Marino lists LaFaro, Haden, Holland, Chambers, Carter, Jormin and peers, and credits Steve Gilmore and Bill Goodwin, with whom he made his first record.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you have a short list of bass players that you said, “I want to sound like that”?
Well I would put Scott LaFaro up there, I’d put Charlie Haden up there, I’d put Dave Holland. Oh there’s so many. Paul Chambers I was really into, Ron Carter, oh there’s a

lot. There’s a lot of great young players. I love the Swedish bass player Anders Jormin – he’s a newer guy now. Mike Formanek speaking of my peers. Steve Respina. Steve Gilmore was a big influence on me because he was part of Phil Woods’ group, also Bill Goodwin. Bill Goodwin – I hooked up with him and we had a guitar trio with our late great friend Vic Juris that was the first record I did was through Bill. That was a really great hook-up for me.
